lead.headline: Mercury's Day: Say It Clean
lead.subhead: Overcast and 63° at 6 AM, drizzle chances near 38%, high near 65. Apple and OpenAI head to court today after a judge gave Apple early access to OpenAI's hiring records. Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. is nursing ribs before the Bears come to town, and the Warriors beat the Lakers in Las Vegas.

articles.hed: Edition XLII: One Day to Get Ready
articles.deck: Box breathing, the 3-minute opener, then a Wednesday for clear messages and a packed bag before tomorrow's flight.
articles.body: Volume XLII is live from Carpentersville on a gray, mild Wednesday (63° at dawn, high near 65, drizzle possible). Thursday's rain is close to certain, and the Vegas flight leaves at 9:03 PM, so today is the day to finish packing. On the AI desk, a federal judge gave Apple early access to OpenAI's interview records with former Apple employees, and the two sides head to court today. OpenAI also said a now-fired employee hid a recording device in one of its offices; the FBI made an arrest. Apple unveiled a new Apple TV 4K built around Siri AI, Anthropic and Workday teamed up at Workday Rising in Las Vegas, and xAI is opening Grok's Voice Mode to everyone with live translation. In football, Monday night's loss is still costing the Rams: the NFL suspended left tackle Alaric Jackson two games and the team cut kicker Harrison Mevis. The Falcons say Penix's rib injury isn't serious, and he may face the Bears on Sunday. Wednesday belongs to Mercury, god of messengers, and Solomon has the right line: a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold. fall down 7 stand up 8.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Gray sky, soft air, the day of Mercury. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Breathe the way you want to speak today: slow, clear, nothing wasted.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the one message that matters.

mindset.body: Petr Yan, defending his belt against Merab Dvalishvili on Oct. 24, put it plainly: pressure is just the other guy's game plan, and 'diamonds are made under pressure.' You've got a packed day before a trip, rain tomorrow, and a lot on the board. Good. Pressure shows you who you are. Today, win the first hour, say the important thing clean and once, and pack before the night gets away from you. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Wednesday: run this right after Morning Charge, breath first and then the body. Mild but damp this morning (low 60s, drizzle possible), so do the RipStick finisher inside or under cover. Mercury's day: keep every rep crisp and exact.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: Judge gives Apple early access to OpenAI hiring records; the two head to court today
items.body: Judge Edward Davila ruled that Apple can see OpenAI's interview materials with former Apple employees who applied to its hardware and robotics groups, plus LINE messages between people named in the case. He denied, for now, Apple's push for OpenAI's research on metal finishes and power management. Apple's preliminary-injunction hearing in the trade-secret case is set for today, 9 AM PT.

items.hed: Anthropic and Workday connect Claude to Sana HR and finance agents
items.body: Announced at Workday Rising in Las Vegas, the partnership lets Workday's Sana agents and Claude work off the same Workday data and controls, inside either Sana or Claude. The Sana in Claude plugin is in early access now and expected to be generally available in late 2026.

items.hed: xAI opens Grok Voice Mode to everyone and adds live translation
items.body: Grok's conversational Voice Mode is now free for all users, with real-time, two-way spoken translation across dozens of languages. The update starts rolling out today in the Grok app and in Tesla vehicles.

items.hed: Warriors beat the Lakers 101-89 in Las Vegas
items.body: Golden State outscored L.A. 51-26 in the second half at T-Mobile Arena. Brandin Podziemski led the Warriors with 17; Austin Reaves had a game-high 28 for the Lakers.
Toronto scored 86 in the first half and won by 50 at Scotiabank Arena. Kawhi Leonard led the Raptors with 21; James Wiseman had 18 for New York. The two meet again Thursday at the Garden.

items.hed: Thunder edge the Pacers 114-112 in overtime
items.body: Tyrese Haliburton scored 24 for Indiana and Jared McCain had 20 for Oklahoma City in the night's closest game. Tonight the Bulls visit the Bucks at 7 PM CT.

items.hed: Falcons: Penix's rib injury not considered serious ahead of the Bears
items.body: Michael Penix Jr. left Sunday's loss to the Ravens after a late hit and sat out overtime. Sources told Adam Schefter he might play Sunday against Chicago, but Atlanta wants to see him practice first; Kevin Stefanski said he'd know more by Wednesday. Tua Tagovailoa is the backup.

items.hed: Ravens' comeback over Atlanta snaps a 581-game streak
items.body: Backup Tyler Huntley led a 71-yard drive in 1:51 to tie it, scored on a 1-yard sneak in overtime, and Kyle Hamilton's interception sealed a 30-23 win. Teams down eight or more in the final minute had lost 581 straight games before Sunday night.

items.hed: Rams lose Alaric Jackson for two games, cut kicker Mevis after Bills loss
items.body: The NFL suspended the left tackle two games for punching Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after Monday's 37-34 overtime loss; David Quessenberry starts against Arizona. The Rams released Harrison Mevis, whose overtime try was blocked, and signed Blake Grupe.

items.hed: Zuffa Boxing signs WBC middleweight champ Carlos Adames
items.body: The Ring's No. 1 middleweight (25-1-1, 18 KOs) signed a multi-fight deal; his Zuffa debut will be announced soon. 'I'm here to make history,' Adames said.

items.hed: Pereira says the UFC 'manipulated' fans into Gane vs. Hokit
items.body: Passed over for a Ciryl Gane rematch, Alex Pereira says the UFC used commentators like Daniel Cormier to sell Gane vs. Josh Hokit for the heavyweight title at UFC 334 (Nov. 14, Madison Square Garden). Pereira faces Sergei Pavlovich on Dec. 12 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

items.hed: Petr Yan: 'Diamonds are made under pressure' before the Dvalishvili trilogy
items.body: The bantamweight champ (20-5) defends against Merab Dvalishvili (21-5) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi. Dvalishvili won their first fight in 2023; Yan took the rematch last year.

Wednesday is Mercury's day in the old planetary week ('mercredi' in French; Woden's day in English, since the Romans matched Odin with Mercury). The Solomonic grimoires give the first hour after sunrise to the day's planet. Mercury rules messengers, speech, writing, trade and learning. Magicians saved that hour for letters, contracts and study. Send your most important message there.

items.hed: The Emerald Tablet: as above, so below
items.body: The Hermetic tradition is named for Hermes Trismegistus, the 'thrice-great' fusion of Greek Hermes (Mercury) and Egyptian Thoth, the scribe of the gods. Its most famous text, the Emerald Tablet, says that what is below is like what is above. The practical reading: the small things you do today should match the big thing you're building. If they don't, change the small things.

items.hed: Thomas, Saying 5: look at what's in front of you
items.body: The Gospel of Thomas says: 'Recognize what is in your sight, and that which is hidden from you will become plain to you. For there is nothing hidden which will not become manifest.' The mystics read it as a rule for insight: stop hunting for secrets and look hard at what's already in front of you. The answer you need is usually sitting on today's list.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.body: Solomon wrote: 'A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver' (Proverbs 25:11). The right words, at the right moment, in the right setting are worth more than a pile of words at the wrong one. On Mercury's day, the day before a trip, the counsel is simple: say less, say it clearly, and say it when it can land.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, write the one message that matters most today in three sentences or fewer. Read it out loud once. Send it in the first hour after sunrise. Then start the 3-minute opener.

lesson.oneLiner: Search where the experts already post.
beats: A search engine ranks pages by popularity. A creator-powered search pulls from people posting about the niche they live in.
Run the same question two ways: Muse for what creators are showing right now, Grok or ChatGPT for the summary and the reasoning.
Use it for 7EightMade research: search your niche (AI agents for small business) and note who is posting and what's landing.
Turn what you find into content: one creator insight can become a story slide or a drop idea.
lesson.takeaway: Ask Muse one real 7EightMade question today, run the same question in Grok, and save the best creator or idea you find.
